title: Eosin whole-brain mount staining to analyze neurodegeneration in a fly model of Alzheimer’s disease
protocol: Anesthetize 50-day old F1 females in a pad with CO2.
Wash flies briefly in 70% ethanol to remove waxy coating.
Transfer flies to a drop of ice-cold PBS in a dissecting chamber.
Decapitate and remove proboscis while in PBS.
Transfer heads to a drop of ice-cold 4% PFA for fixation.
Fix heads for 15 minutes in the drop of 4% PFA.
Dissect brains in a new drop of ice-cold 4% PFA in the dissecting chamber.
Place brains in a 74 μm mesh netwell inside a 12-well plate containing washing buffer.
Wash brains 2 times in 0.1% PBT for 30 min each at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Wash brains 1 time in PBS for 30 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Add 2 mL of Eosin into a clean well.
Transfer the netwell with the brains to the eosin.
Stain brains for 3 min at room temperature and gentle agitation.
Wash brains 2 times in PBS for 30 minutes each at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Wash brains 1 time in 0.1% PBT for 10 minutes at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Wash brain 1 time in 0.1% PBT overnight at 4°C with gentle agitation.
Place the brains on a printed slide in a drop of VECTASHIELD.
Pick one brain at a time under the scope using tweezers by lifting it from underneath and place it in a drop of mounting media in the desired well.
Orient the brains in the desired way, with the back of the brain facing the coverslip.
Add a coverslip to seal the preparation with nail polish.
Keep mounted slides covered at 4°C for at least 4 months prior to imaging.
Image brains using the 488 nm laser.
Acquire images with 1024 × 1024 pixels and 8-bit resolution.
Use 40× magnification to visualize vacuoles and other brain structures.
Install Fiji/CheeseMaker Tool Timing: 5 min
Download and Install Fiji

Update Fiji and install plugins: Help > Update... > Manage Update Sites, click checkboxes for 3D ImageJ Suite, BoneJ, clij, clij2, clij-assistant, clij-assistant-extensions, IJPB-plugins, close window, apply changes
Download the CheeseMaker Tool from GitHub repository
Open decompressed folder CheeseMaker-main
Click file “CheeseMaker.ijm” to open
Move up one level to the folder “Fiji.App”.
Click on the folder “macros”, then click on “toolsets”.
Save the plugin, macro, or script in the appropriate location.
Close Fiji and reopen it to complete installation.
Click on the toolbar button at the far right: “More Tools”.
Select “>>” from the options and click “CheeseMaker”.
A new button should appear on the Fiji Tools Bar: “CheeseMaker tool”.
Open an image in Fiji.
Click on the CheeseMaker Tool button located at the Toolbar.
A window will pop-up saying “Define the ROI using a selection tool”.
Click on the desired selection tool from the Toolbar and define a ROI in the image.
Click “Ok” on the Cheese Selector window.
The CheeseMaker tool will process and analyze the image in the defined ROI.
Save the results and the images of interest.
Close all opened images.
Open a new image and repeat steps 2 through 6 in this section.
Convert images to 8-bit in ImageJ if acquired with other bits per pixel settings.
Activate the CheeseMaker Tool in ImageJ.
Select an area of interest for segmentation.
Threshold pixels where the ratio of staining signal/Gaussian background (sigmax=30.5, sigmay=30.5, sigmaz=10.0) is below 0.3 to segment areas with no or very low eosin staining.
Apply three rounds of dilation and erosion (Morphological Closing) to every thresholded pixel.
Consider a vacuole as five nearby pixels in the shape of a cross that are black, removing isolated non-black pixels and smoothing edges by closing narrow gaps between proximal thresholded areas.
